sentences.text: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 08-01-2023 at about 8.00 p.m., the petitioner was riding his motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-W-2610, on Parashurampura-Dharmapura road, near Parashurampura Forest, Chitradurga, carefully and cautiously, by observing the traffic rules and regulations.

At that time, all of a sudden one passenger auto bearing No.KA-16-D-4293, driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, with high speed, came from Doddachelluru road and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Parashurampura and Chitradurga Hospital, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bengaluru,
wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident he was shepherd and earning a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- per annum.
But, due to accidental injuries he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Parashurampura Police have registered the case against the driver of the said passenger auto for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of auto- rickshaw bearing No.KA-16-D-4293 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.

It has contended that, the vehicle in question i.e. auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-16-D-4293 is not at all involved in the alleged accident, the same has been falsely implicated in order to get wrongful gain and to make wrongful loss to respondent No.1.

The entire police records are manipulated by showing the registration number of auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-16-D-4293 and seasoned professional have joined hands with the petitioner and manipulated the charge-sheet.

Further it is contended that, the petitioner has suppressed the true facts and colluded with the respondent No.2 and the jurisdictional police and fixed false case against the driver of auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-16-D-4293.

As per the police records there is delay in lodging complaint, the jurisdictional police have filed a false charge-sheet,
by creating a false story and implicated the present vehicle and manipulated records.

Further it is Shivashankar K.T vs Future India Gen Ins Co Ltd on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160093543/
2 contended that, at the time of alleged accident, the petitioner was not wearing safety headgear and it is violation of Motor Vehicles Act.

No.KA- 16-D-4293 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?

13.

At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
the issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.1 in respect of offending auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-16- D-4293 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

The respondent No.1 & 2 have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the insured auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-16-D-4293 was not at all involved in the alleged accident, the same has been falsely implicated by the petitioner, in order to get wrongful gain and to make wrongful loss to the respondents.
But, the respondents have failed to establish the said contentions.

They have neither adduced any evidence to establish the above contentions, nor they have produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Even, the respondents No.1 and 2 have not stepped into witness box to depose the contentions taken in their written statements on oath.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-16-D- 4293 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the petitioner from opposite direction, while he was proceeding on the left side of Parashurampura-Dharmapura road.

Though, the learned counsel for respondents No.1 and 2 have cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part, in the cause of accident.

14. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazer and Ex.P.4 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the left side of 12 feet wide Parashurampura- Dharmapura road, near Parashurampura Forest, Challakere Taluk, in between the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-W- 2610 and offending auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-16- D-4293.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.5, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
On the other hand, the respondents have not produced any rebuttal evidence to show that, the said documents are false and concocted documents.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.7 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending auto- rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-16-D-4293 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-16-D-4293.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

i) Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.15.
As per Ex.P.15, the date of birth of the petitioner is 10-06-1993.
The accident has taken place on 08-01-2023 at about 8:00 p.m.
This clearly goes show that, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 30 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor, who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered 1) right femur shaft fracture open Type-II, 2) right foot crush injury with right ankle and subtalar joint dislocation with open Type-III C and

3)
right pan brachial plexus injury right DER fracture and for the said injuries the petitioner has undergone surgery.
Further, he has deposed that, the right sided B/K has been amputee at M/3rd level of the right leg.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered disability of right upper limb (Pan brachial plexus injury) and functionless dangling limb held by the side of the Trunk to the extent of 90% and right below knee at M/3rd level to the extent of 65%, united fracture shaft of femur with implants in situ disability of 5%, in total he has suffered 70% disability to the right lower limb.

Further, the Ex.P.8 and 9 discharge summaries (total 2), Ex.P.16 OPD card and Ex.P.17 x-ray also clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries and he has undergone surgery for the said injuries.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the disability assessed by him are against the guidelines issued by the Central Government and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability suffered by the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 08-01-2023 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 07-11- 2024, which is after lapse of one year and 11 months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires to undergo surgeries for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

sentences.text: Hence, in the instant case the disability of 70% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was a shepherd and was earning a sum of Rs.6,00,000/- per annum.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondents have specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before the accident he was a shepherd and was earning Rs.6,00,000/- per annum.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in the year 2023.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,86,000/-.
b) As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 30 years is 17.

viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 30 years and unfortunately he has suffered 1) right femur shaft fracture open Type-II, 2) right foot crush injury with right ankle and subtalar joint dislocation with open Type-III C and 3) right pan brachial plexus injury right DER fracture.

ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo surgeries for removal of implants and the estimate of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/-.

Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

21. Liability: Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-16-D- 4293.
It is not in dispute that, the policy issued by the respondent No.1 bearing No.V9969110, in respect of offending auto-rickshaw was valid from 24-03-2022 to 23- 03-2023.
As such the policy issued by the respondent No.1 in respect of offending vehicle was valid as on the date of accident.
Further, there is no evidence on record to show that, there is any breach of terms and conditions of said policy by the insurer/respondent No.2.
The evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that,
due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-16-D-4293 the said accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.26,54,636/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.50,000/-), from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.1, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
22. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.26,54,636/- (Rupees twenty six lakh fifty four thousand six hundred and thirty six only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.50,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.1 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
